comments.author: @yuan267
comments.text:
What a beautiful place. This has always been one of my dream countries to visit. Deep down, I know it may be impossible for me to afford a trip there, but somehow it still gives me hope.

I always tell myself that if the day comes when God asks my soul where I would like to travel, I would choose this place without hesitation.

Just watching this video fills me with a sense of peace that I can't really explain. Maybe it's because the country I live in feels so chaotic, and seeing a place this calm and beautiful reminds me that somewhere in the world, life can feel slower, quieter, and more peaceful.

For now, I'll keep dreaming. Sometimes, even watching a beautiful place from afar is enough to bring a little peace to my heart.

replies.author: @ThePlanetJournalGlobe
replies.text: Thank you so much for your heartfelt comment, @yuan267. We are truly moved to know that our documentary brought a sense of peace to your heart. Travel isn't just about the physical journey; it’s also about the connection and hope we find through these stories. Never stop dreaming—we’re so glad we could share a piece of Scotland’s tranquility with you today.

comments.author: @main11gear
comments.text: I've been to Scotland twice. Once for 15 days (late may into June) without a drop of rain, temperatures between 70 - 75 degrees (F) in the daytime and mid 50s at night. Absolutely awesome! Two full weeks of awesome weather. Then went back last year for my friends wedding in August. AUGUST! The highs were in the 40s - 50s (F) in Braemar where the wedding war performed. We didn't even take jackets. Living in the US, who would have ever thought you need a jacket in August?

replies.author: @ThePlanetJournalGlobe
replies.text:
@main11gear
What a great story! Scottish weather is definitely unpredictable, and Braemar can be quite chilly even in summer. Thanks for sharing your experience—it’s a great reminder to always pack a jacket for Scotland!
